assumptions: For the conformal result, model and candidate generator frozen before calibration; calibration and next chemical systems exchangeable as whole groups.
For global stability, finite panels must contain all admissible competing phases; otherwise outputs are panel-relative.
Target fidelity, composition normalization, thermodynamic condition, and elemental references must match across calibration and target.
For the deterministic robust LP result, non-affine phase residuals lie in supplied independent intervals.
Calibration reference labels are held out from predictor fitting, model selection, panel-generation tuning, and delta selection.
contract.interface: Finite phase panel with rational normalized composition vectors, per-atom energy predictions, signed target-removed hull margins, calibration reference energies by whole chemical system, and optional secondary objective-property intervals.

costs.high_fidelity_energy: Reference energies for full calibration panels and relevant test phases; dominates runtime.
costs.system_calibration: At least 19 exchangeable calibration systems for a finite 95% split-conformal order statistic; much larger samples may be needed for a useful margin.
costs.optimization: Hull or exact LP computation polynomial in panel size and encoded input; preserve primal/dual witnesses and roundoff bounds.
costs.structure_search: Complete structure/composition generation or a lower bound for omitted phases remains uncharged and unresolved.

candidate.representation: For each non-elemental target i in a finite phase panel, use signed margin d_i=e_i-min_lambda lambda^T e_comp over all mass-balanced competitor mixtures; for system g score S_g=max over all target candidates in T_g of |d_gi-dhat_gi|.
candidate.hypothesis: A maximum-score split-conformal quantile over exchangeable whole chemical systems yields simultaneous 1-delta marginal hull-margin coverage for all candidates in a new declared phase panel; balanced reaction scores cancel shared affine composition errors.

missing_lemma: A useful, honest exchangeability class for whole chemical systems and evidence that reaction-margin conformal calibration improves the number of candidates certified over phasewise conformal intervals or CAL at equal high-fidelity query cost; global phase completeness remains a separate missing premise.
comparator: Convex hull-aware active learning (CAL); nominal seven-facet or graph model; phasewise conformal intervals plus simultaneous correction and robust interval hull LP.
falsifier_or_next_experiment: Freeze predictor and structure candidate generator; calibrate and hold out complete chemical systems; compare all four methods at matched PBE/r2SCAN energy budget; measure simultaneous hull-label coverage, certified-candidate count, false-stable rate, and compute calls. Reject advantage if coverage fails or no certification gain at matched coverage/cost.
